articles.headline: Week 3 NFL highlights: Best plays, moments, touchdowns, more
articles.description: Sunday of Week 3 features 14 games, including an international game in Rio de Janeiro between the Ravens and Cowboys.
articles.body:
Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season continued Sunday with 14 games, including nine in the early window, and we'll have the best highlights, touchdowns and moments from all of them.

In the early window, New York Jets coach Aaron Glenn returned to face his former team in the Detroit Lions, and Tennessee Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll is facing off against the team that fired him during the season last year, the New York Giants.

The Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys will take their talents to Rio de Janeiro in one of four games in the second window before the Denver Broncos host the Los Angeles Rams in primetime to cap off the day.

Here are the top plays from Sunday, and be sure to keep checking back once the afternoon games and "Sunday Night Football" kick off.

Week 3 highlights

articles.headline: Deshaun Watson wins over Browns' fans with performance in win
articles.description: One month after Browns fans booed him in a preseason game, Deshaun Watson gave the Cleveland faithful something to cheer about in their home opener.
articles.body:
BEREA, Ohio -- One month after Cleveland Browns fans booed him in the second half of a preseason game, Deshaun Watson gave the Cleveland faithful something to cheer about in their home opener.

Watson led a game-winning drive for the second consecutive game, throwing a 14-yard touchdown to tight end Harold Fannin Jr. with 1:48 left in the Browns' 21-18 win over the Carolina Panthers on Sunday.

Cleveland is 2-1 and tied for first place in the AFC North ahead of a "Thursday Night Football" home game against the 2-1 Pittsburgh Steelers. Watson completed 16 of 30 passes for 144 yards and two touchdowns. He also ran for 45 yards on 11 carries.

In leading Cleveland to another come-from-behind victory, Watson became the first Browns quarterback since Baker Mayfield in Weeks 14 and 15 of the 2018 season to lead game-winning touchdown drives in the fourth quarter of consecutive games, according to ESPN Research.

"The moment I woke up, the anticipation, the anxiousness, everything. Just [to] get in front of the fans, just to get here, and get started. I wanted to play perfect so bad," Watson said. "It's the NFL. That's the way the game's going to go: ups and downs. The energy, the fans, it was amazing. They kept believing in us, they kept the energy up. I know there was a little lull in the game, but that's going to happen. But overall, we didn't give up and we fed off their energy.

"We continued to feed off that energy of the crowd, and we wanted to make a special play. I told the guys in the huddle, 'Man just [believe] in me and I'm going to use my legs.' Whenever that play comes up, make that play, and Harold did."

Watson and the Browns went 65 yards over eight plays on the game-winning drive. He converted two third downs, once on a 21-yard run and then the decisive touchdown pass. Watson also converted a two-point attempt with a completion to rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston.

A roughing the passer penalty helped the drive by negating an interception but forced Watson to miss one play. Shedeur Sanders entered for Watson and completed his lone pass to running back Quinshon Judkins for no gain before Watson returned.

"I just lost my breath. I guess they thought it was my head," Watson said.

Cleveland's defense ended the game with one final stop, a Ronnie Hickman interception on Bryce Young with nine seconds remaining.

Watson's late-game heroics helped overshadow a slow start for the Browns' offense that lasted three quarters. Cleveland led 10-9 entering the fourth quarter, but Watson was 10-for-21 for 67 yards and a touchdown.

The potential reaction from Browns fans was a topic of discussion in Cleveland in the lead-up to the home opener after Watson was booed in the second half of a preseason home game against the Buffalo Bills; afterward, he called the booing "personal" and "disrespectful." Days later, Watson said his "emotions got the best of me." On Wednesday, he said he was "ready for support" in his first home game of the season.

articles.headline: NFL Week 3's best arrivals, led by Davante Adams
articles.description: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
articles.body:
The official start of fall means it's fit season, when players start dominating the gameday tunnels with eye-popping jackets, sweaters and pants.

Last week, the Philadelphia Eagles played a blazing hot game in Nashville that had players' cleats melting with with temperatures of up to 157 degrees Fahrenheit on the turf. 

Hopefully this week is the start of a heat decline with more cloudier 50-to-75 degree days ahead to allow players to comfortably show off their fits.

To kick off Week 3, Green Bay Packers quarterbacks Jordan Love and Tyrod Taylor rocked my two favorite outfits of the Thursday primetime slate.

Love came in shining -- literally -- with a Public School New York x KAY jewelry collaboration jacket: the definition of a statement piece.

Meanwhile, Taylor's Dries Van Noten sweater is the perfect kickoff to fall -- warm but fashion-forward. There are so many fabric design details within this one piece, showing the value of layers.

As always, Sunday is where the big show begins. Here are Week 3 fits that caught our eye:

Sunday's best

For primetime show, it's a who wore it better. The Los Angeles Rams duo of Davante Adams and Byron Young went with all-denim jacket and pant combos. Both can't miss ahead of "Sunday Night Football."

The Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys brought their contrasting styles to Maracanã Stadium for the NFL's first game in Rio de Janeiro. Lamar Jackson donned a graphic tee paying homage to the late rapper DMX, while George Pickens' fit featured Brazil's national colors in a nod to the host country. 

San Francisco 49ers safety Malik Mustapha styling with an eye-popping Kid Super jacket was my favorite of this window.

From Stefon Diggs' black jacket covered in NBA throwback logo patches, to Malik Nabers' custom "H1M" pendant, players brought plenty of style and personality ahead of the early slate.

Four standouts in this window included Los Angeles Chargers cornerback Donte Jackson 's Boardwalk Vintage fit, which completed a preppy rockstar vibe. Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young KITH x New York to the world jersey was a winner. Cleveland Browns running back Quinshon Judkins leaned into the Fall Cleveland vibes with this unique Celine sweater. I love retro call backs so must give Diggs love on his vintage NBA bomber jacket.

Thursday night fashion

The Green Bay Packers host the Atlanta Falcons to kick off Week 3's slate, and quarterback Jordan Love entered the home opener in style, pairing an oversize studded leather pullover with black trousers, a crisp white shirt and black tie. He completed the look with dark sunglasses and a checkered duffel bag.

articles.headline: RB Breece Hall suffers thigh injury as Jets lose late once again
articles.description: Jets running back Breece Hall suffered an injury to his right thigh late in Sunday's loss to the Lions.
articles.body:
DETROIT -- Running back Breece Hall, speaking softly to a group of reporters, captured the postgame mood in the New York Jets' locker room on Sunday.

"You know, it sucks, but it's part of the game," he said. "It sucks."

Hall could've been talking about how the Jets lost in the final minutes for the second straight week, falling 31-24 to the Detroit Lions at Ford Field, but he was addressing his injured right thigh.

Early in the fourth quarter, Hall was tackled out of bounds and, rolling over his pain, clutched his right thigh. It was a sobering sight for the Jets (1-2), who found a second-half groove on offense but now face the prospect of moving forward without one of their top weapons.

"I felt something when I was running and then got tackled and planted and then felt something else," said Hall, adding that he probably will have an MRI on Monday. "So, we'll see."

A long-term injury to Hall would be a huge blow to the Jets, who have a litany of injuries on offense.

They played without wide receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger) and tight end Mason Taylor (thumb), forcing them to use players from the practice squad. Left guard Dylan Parham (knee) was injured in the game and didn't return. Wide receiver Garrett Wilson missed the final play of the game while he was evaluated for a concussion, but he cleared protocol and is "fine," according to coach Aaron Glenn.

Despite being short-handed, the Jets rallied from a 24-10 deficit in the fourth quarter on Geno Smith's second and third touchdown passes. They tied it on Wilson's acrobatic, falling-backward catch from 23 yards with 4:06 remaining, but the defense melted in crunch time.

It provided little resistance as Jared Goff led the Lions on a four-play, 65-yard drive, thanks to two wide-open receivers -- Isaac TeSlaa (49 yards) and Jahmyr Gibbs (11-yard touchdown).

A week ago, the Jets blew a 10-point lead in the fourth quarter and lost in overtime to the Green Bay Packers, 20-17.

"We feel like we could easily be 3-0 right now," tight end Jeremy Ruckert said.

At the interview podium, Glenn held up his right hand and, with his thumb and index finger a few inches apart.

"It's this gap right here that we have to close," he said, pointing to the gap with his left hand. "And we're fighting our asses off to close that gap, and we will -- from a coaching perspective and from a player perspective."

The Jets had the momentum after Wilson's touchdown, but they went to a soft zone on defense and left TeSlaa uncovered on a deep over route. The closest defenders were linebacker Jamien Sherwood and cornerback Brandon Stephens.

"I'm not going to blame anything on that," Glenn said. "They just did a really good job of executing their offense on that."

On a third-and-5 from the 11, Glenn sent Jarvis Brownlee Jr. on a slot blitz. It appeared that Brownlee was supposed to cover Gibbs out of the backfield, but he reacted too late. Gibbs was wide open and it was an easy pitch and catch for the game-winning scor

articles.headline: C.J. Stroud says winless Texans will get struggles fixed
articles.description: C.J. Stroud boldly stated that the winless Texans will turn their season around after a 19-17 loss to the previously winless Colts on Sunday.
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- C.J. Stroud boldly stated that the winless Texans will turn their season around after a 19-17 loss to the previously winless Colts on Sunday.

Stroud said the Texans' confidence isn't wavering despite an 0-3 start for a team that has Super Bowl hopes.

"No excuses," Stroud said. "No one cares about what happened. They just want to see if you won or loss. We know who we are in our locker room. We can get this fixed and we will."

The Texans dropped to 0-3 for a second straight year after losing to the Colts on a last-second field goal. Two of the three losses this season have come on the last drive; last year, all three losses came on the final possession of the game.

On Sunday, a questionable decision from coach DeMeco Ryans toward the end of the game cost the Texans potential time for their offense to get into field goal range. 

With 1:11 remaining, Colts running back Jonathan Taylor had a 5-yard carry on first-and-10 from the Houston 45. When Taylor was tackled, the clock read 1:05, but Ryans didn't call a timeout until 29 seconds remained. Two plays later, the Colts had a run for minus-1 yard and a Keenan Allen reception for 5 yards, forcing a fourth down as Houston called its remaining timeouts.

Spencer Shrader nailed a 53-yard field goal for Indy with 16 seconds left, leaving Houston's offense with almost no time to get into field goal range. Stroud ended the afternoon with a Hail Mary attempt from his own 48-yard line that fell out of bounds.

Ryans didn't provide an explanation into his thought process on the timeout call. 

"If I can make a better decision, I'll look at that and try to see where I can make a better decision," he said. "I got multiple people in my ear, but everything starts with me."

The Texans joined the Buccaneers (strike-shortened 1982-83 season) as the only NFL teams to start 0-3 and make the playoffs and then start 0-3 the following season, according to ESPN Research.

On Sunday, the offense was held to a season-low 233 yards. Pro Bowl wideout Nico Collins was again out with a hamstring injury. Stroud finished with 167 passing yards and one touchdown, and the rushing attack produced only 70 yards on 21 carries.

But Collins is close to returning - a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter earlier Sunday that he has "a decent chance" to be back in Week 4 vs. the Dallas Cowboys -- along with other starters for Houston, part of why Stroud feels Houston will save its season.

"We're getting guys back from injury," Stroud said. "I think they'll help. I also like the fight that I've seen with our team. I believe we're not far off, but also it doesn't feel that way because we're 0-3. I have the utmost confidence. You can call me crazy but I don't care."

articles.headline: Steelers' Warren dominates Bengals with career-best 176 yards
articles.description: Steelers RB Jaylen Warren exploded for a career-best 176 yards from scrimmage in a dominant display for Pittsburgh's run game in Sunday's win.
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH -- Just as he had all afternoon, Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren cut through the Cincinnati Bengals' defense off left guard Mason McCormick. Then, with his signature acceleration, Warren burst through the second level and slipped past safety Kyle Dugger and cornerback Tacario Davis.

The only thing separating Warren from the end zone and a fourth-quarter, go-ahead touchdown was 20 yards of open grass.

But after taking a step that sent field turf flying as he crossed the 15-yard line, Warren started to lose his balance. With his arms flailing as he tried -- and failed -- to catch himself, Warren tripped to a stop at Cincinnati's 6-yard line.

The premature ending of that 26-yard run was the only self-inflicted blemish on Warren's career outing in the Steelers' 30-27 win against the Bengals.

"Jaylen's so slippery back there," quarterback Aaron Rodgers said Sunday. "First guy rarely brings him down. He actually brings himself down more than the first guy."

 

Warren, who had 150 yards from scrimmage in the first two weeks combined, finished with a career-best 176 yards from scrimmage. He averaged 7.5 yards per carry, picking up 127 yards -- including 53 after first contact -- on 17 carries.

"I don't even really be making moves," Warren said Sunday. "People just bounce off of me. It's been like that since I was eight years old."

Warren also caught three passes for 49 yards. His numbers would've been even more gaudy if not for a holding penalty against wide receiver DK Metcalf that wiped away an 87-yard run midway through the first quarter.

"I always knew he was a hard runner, but I thought he ran his ass off today, and I'm very proud of him," said guard Brock Hoffman, who made his first start of the season Sunday alongside rookie right tackle Max Iheanachor, who was also making his first start.

Not only did Hoffman and Iheanachor's addition to the starting lineup help invigorate the run game, but the offensive line and the running backs also had a meeting on Monday after the Week 2 loss to New England to get on the same page. That set the table for Sunday's explosion.

"That meeting on Monday was really important for us to just have [the running backs] trust us a little bit more," left tackle Troy Fautanu said. "And obviously shout out to Jaylen for doing what he did today. Just even imagine if Rico [Dowdle] was in there too, what we could have done."

Through the first two weeks of the season, Warren rotated series with Dowdle, but with Dowdle inactive because of a toe injury sustained in the loss to the Patriots, Warren played a career-high 89.8% of offensive snaps -- and he did it while battling a shoulder injury. Warren missed practice on Wednesday and was limited both Thursday and Friday.

"He was the focal point," coach Mike McCarthy said of Warren's impact on the game. "You guys are at practice, you can see how he was limited in certain things. He came up big. He was huge for us today."

articles.headline: Parma part ways with ex-Arsenal assistant Carlos Cuesta
articles.description: Parma parted ways with coach Carlos Cuesta on Sunday after winning only one of their opening five Serie A matches.
articles.headlineJa: パルマ、元アーセナル助監督のカルロス・クエスタ氏と契約解除
articles.descriptionJa: パルマはセリエA開幕5試合でわずか1勝にとどまり、日曜日にカルロス・クエスタ監督と解任・退任の道を歩むこととなった。
articles.body:
Parma parted ways with coach Carlos Cuesta on Sunday after winning only one of their opening five Serie A matches.

The club said Cuesta "has been relieved of his duty" and that "following an internal discussion between the club and coach, it was agreed that the conditions in order to continue this working relationship and the advancement of the sporting project, were not being met. Both parties came to a mutual agreement."

- Goals galore! Why Barça's start to season is best in Europe's top leagues for almost 100 years

- Udinese sign former Real Madrid defender Alaba

- Havertz back at Arsenal for injury treatment

A replacement was not immediately named.

Parma beat Genoa last weekend but only have four points.

Cuesta became the youngest manager in Europe's top five leagues, and the youngest Serie A manager in almost a century, when he was appointed by Parma in June 2025 at the age of 29. He had previously spent five years as assistant to Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta.

Having decided at a young age that his future lay in coaching rather than playing, Cuesta was given his first chance at Atlético Madrid with their underage teams and after four years there, went travelling Europe to study coaching methods.

It was during this period that Cuesta met Arteta, then part of Pep Guardiola's coaching staff at Manchester City, and after a two-year spell with Juventus' youth academy, Cuesta joined Arsenal in 2020.

He guided Parma to a 13th-place finish last season.

It's the third coaching change in Serie A this season after Paolo Vanoli replaced Fabio Grosso at Fiorentina and Raffaele Palladino replaced Domenico Tedesco at Bologna.

Parma's next match is at Serie A champions Inter Milan on Oct. 10 after the international break.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.
